chunks: Ali ibn al-Hasan narrated from Muhammad and Ahmad, the two sons of al-Hasan, from their father, from al-Qasim ibn 'Urayrah, from 'Abdullah ibn Bukayr, from Zurarah, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

I said to him, 'A man gave his wife the option [of divorce].' He said, 'The option belongs to both of them as long as they remain in their session [of marriage/negotiation]; but when they separate, there is no option for either of them.'

key_terms.مَجلِسِهِمَا: their session / place of sitting together

ai.seo_question: When does the wife's option of divorce expire if the husband grants it?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Isfahani’s chain clarifies the temporal boundary of *khayar al-talaq* (option of divorce), emphasizing that the right is tied to the physical continuity of the marital session (*majlis*) rather than a fixed duration. In Shia jurisprudence, this establishes that separation breaks the legal link, preventing either party from exercising the option after the fact, thereby ensuring clarity in marital status. This ruling underscores the importance of immediate action in divorce proceedings to avoid ambiguity in the wife's status.
